entries.text: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after two stories about an affair with subordinate Kimberly Powell and a board meeting to consider his ouster were published on Wednesday.
The resignation marks the departure of one of Silicon Valley’s most powerful executives.
The event follows earlier allegations that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy and that Nvidia’s Southeast Asian buyer Megaspeed may have been involved in illicit GPU sales.
Huang had claimed in May that Nvidia held zero percent market share in China after U.S. export controls on its high‑end chips.
Short‑seller Culper Research contradicted that, estimating over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenue still came from China through illegal diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.
Megaspeed, identified as Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, showed no visible activity when The Straits Times visited its Singapore office a month earlier.
The Verge’s coverage also notes that newly elected Democrats are questioning who knew what and when about these China‑related dealings.
Nvidia dominates the AI hardware market, making its ties to China a matter of national security for the United States.

OpenAI launched a ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November 2026 that lets its Dots agents shop and check out for users.
The feature is initially limited to U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 or older who have an eligible U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, American Express or Chase card.
Users must approve each purchase with a biometric security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint.
After adding a payment card, the wallet creates a payment token that replaces the actual card details during transactions, so the AI agent never sees the card number.
The merchant receives only the token, shipping address and contact information needed to fulfill the order.
problems: model check: The source says the merchant gets shipping info but does NOT receive the payment token; the token is not shared with the merchant, contradicting the claim.

entries.text: Users retain credit‑card rewards and can dispute transactions, as the purchase still uses the original card’s protections.
OpenAI plans future controls like spending limits and category restrictions to give users more autonomy over agent‑made purchases.
AI‑driven personal assistants are expanding beyond recommendations to direct transactions, a trend seen with services like Meta’s Muse and Instinct that already support AI‑assisted shopping.
OpenAI’s entry follows earlier launches of its Dots agents platform earlier in the year, aiming to test the feature with a small user base before broader rollout.
The wallet mirrors existing mobile payment systems such as Apple Pay and Google Wallet, which also use tokenisation for security.

On Thursday, 12 pm ET, users reported Outlook failures and Microsoft confirmed a widespread outage affecting Microsoft 365 services worldwide.
Within an hour the problem spread to more than 70 countries, shutting down email, Teams, and other tools for tens of millions of users.
Microsoft later said the incident stemmed from a network‑capacity upgrade issue, not a cyberattack or AI agent.
The outage lasted roughly 24 hours, with most services restored by the following day but some subsystems still recovering.
Microsoft increased email queue time to 48 hours to ensure delayed messages are eventually delivered.
Independent researcher Jonathan Leitschuh warned users to expect a flood of notifications as systems come back online.
Governments, airlines, law‑enforcement agencies, and hospitals all reported operational disruptions during the downtime.
Microsoft 365 provides core productivity tools for businesses, governments, and individuals, making it a single point of failure for many critical workflows.
problems: model check: Source describes the outage scope but does not state Microsoft 365 is a single point of failure for critical workflows.

Nvidia announced on 12 November 2026 that chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim chief executive officer after Jensen Huang resigned amid a personal scandal.

entries.text: The board of directors made the appointment public on a Thursday, naming Kress as the successor while an independent investigation into Huang’s conduct begins.
problems: model check: Investigation was announced later (Sunday), not concurrently as claim implies

entries.text: Harvey Jones, newly appointed chair of Nvidia’s board, said Kress will be supported by an experienced leadership team and that the board has full confidence in her abilities.
Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 and has been described as a key figure in the company’s extraordinary growth, with deep knowledge of its products, customers, operations and finances.
Former Nvidia executives note her strong‑willed, professional and whip‑smart demeanor, and her ability to understand Jensen Huang’s thinking style.

Analysts such as Patrick Moorhead call her the logical choice because she answers hard questions directly and has credibility with investors, going beyond typical CFO duties to engage with product road‑maps from rack‑scale systems to networking and software.
The board also launched an independent investigation following a New York Times report linking Huang’s affair to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Nvidia, a leading chipmaker, has faced heightened scrutiny after revelations that its co‑founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with a woman believed to be linked to China’s Ministry of State Security.
The scandal prompted the board to replace Huang and to bring in a crisis communications firm earlier in the year to manage press inquiries.
Kress’s appointment aims to provide stability for investors and employees while the company navigates the investigation and potential regulatory fallout.
